title: From X-ray to pixel: inside a digital sensor
topic: How a digital intraoral sensor turns X-ray photons into gray-level pixels, layer by layer, and how a PSP plate does it differently.

claims.claim: Layer stack of a solid-state sensor: housing, scintillator, fiber-optic plate, CMOS chip, read-out electronics + ADC (schematic model of one sensor design, not to scale)
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen), Fig. 4-3 caption (manufacturer-supplied figure). Not every sensor has a fiber-optic plate (W&P: scintillator 'coated directly on the CCD surface or coupled to the surface by fiberoptics')

claims.claim: Scintillator: X-ray -> visible light; CsI or Gd oxysulfide
claims.source: Function: White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction). Materials: Farman TT et al., Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol Endod 2005;99:608-13 (PMID 15829886), abstract (thallium-doped CsI and terbium-doped gadolinium oxysulfide screens on an intraoral CCD). Board note: the W&P 7e solid-state paragraph prints 'gadolinium oxybromide compounds... or cesium iodide'
White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction), Fig. 4-3 / 4-4 captions (fiber-optics couple the scintillator to the chip)

claims.claim: CMOS chip: light -> charge; transistors per pixel
claims.source: White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction) ('charge in each pixel proportional to the exposure'; 'each pixel is... directly connected to a transistor'); plural per Arvanitis et al., Med Phys 2007;34:4612-25 (PMID 18196789), abstract ('standard three transistor CMOS active pixel sensor', bench mammography detector)
White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction) (analog-to-digital conversion; 'Current digital detectors capture data at 8, 10, 12, or 16 bits')

claims.claim: Image: number -> gray level. Toy model / schematic: 36 x 27 charge wells and a procedurally drawn periapical; more exposure = fuller well = darker pixel; well heights and the row-by-row build-up are illustrative
claims.source: White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction) (charge packets proportional to exposure; display convention); no measured values shown

claims.claim: PSP plate (Eu-doped barium fluorohalide): X-rays -> trapped electrons
claims.source: White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction) ('europium-doped' barium fluorohalide; trapped electrons = latent image); Leblans et al., Materials (Basel) 2011;4:1034-86 (PMID 28879966), abstract ('Absorbed X-ray energy is stored in crystal defects'; medical computed-radiography review, no dental content); Kamburoğlu et al., Imaging Sci Dent 2022;52:93-101 (PMID 35387105), PMC full text (dental paper: PSP crystals 'contain europium doped barium fluorohalides')

claims.claim: Red laser -> blue-violet light -> photomultiplier (schematic scanner; exposure and read-out drawn as two separate steps)
claims.source: Leblans et al., Materials (Basel) 2011;4:1034-86 (PMID 28879966): abstract ('set free as blue photons'); PMC full text ('A red laser beam is moved over the plate'; 'characteristic 390 nm luminescence'; 'UV to blue Eu2+ emission'; light guide to a photomultiplier tube). 'Blue-violet' is the reel's word for that blue, 390 nm-peak emission; neither source prints the compound word; IAEA, Diagnostic Radiology Physics handbook 2014, Ch. 7 ('usually blue'); White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction) (red laser, fiber-optics to a photomultiplier tube). Board note: W&P 7e prints 'green spectrum between 300 and 500 nm' for the emitted light

claims.claim: End card. Sensor (CMOS, CCD): image in seconds, rigid. PSP plate: thin, film-sized, wide latitude (source line says in vitro), needs a scanner
claims.source: Kamburoğlu et al., Imaging Sci Dent 2022;52:93-101 (PMID 35387105), PMC full text (said of CMOS: 'available to view in a matter of seconds after the exposure'; CMOS 'bulky and rigid'; plates 'the same shape and dimensions of conventional films'; 'thinner nature of PSP sensors'); White & Pharoah 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 (textbook, online reproduction) (solid-state detectors: 'rapid availability of the image after exposure', 'sensor bulk'; film-like handling of plates; laser scanner). CCD speed: Mouyen et al., Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1989;68:238-42 (PMID 2780024), abstract (RVG, a CCD unit, produces 'an image immediately after exposure'). 'Wide latitude', in vitro: Berkhout et al., Dentomaxillofac Radiol 2004;33:1-5 (PMID 15140814), abstract (also warns of unnecessarily high dose); Borg et al., Dentomaxillofac Radiol 2000;29:70-5 (PMID 10808218), abstract. Deliberately not 'wider than sensors': Farman & Farman, Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol Endod 2005;99:485-9 (PMID 15772598); Marinho-Vieira et al., Dentomaxillofac Radiol 2023;52:20220370 (PMID 36988093), abstracts

caption:
From X-ray to pixel: a sensor, taken apart.
A scintillator (CsI or Gd oxysulfide) turns X-rays into light. In some sensors a fiber-optic plate guides it to the CMOS chip, where each pixel stores charge. The ADC turns charge into a number, shown as gray.
PSP plates trap electrons: red laser in, blue-violet light out, bright light erases. Latitude is wide in vitro (can hide overexposure), not always wider than today's sensors.
Boards: W&P 7e says "Gd oxybromide" and "green" PSP light.
Schematic animation.
Refs: White & Pharoah 7e (textbook); Farman TT 2005, OOOOE; Leblans 2011, Materials; Berkhout 2004, Marinho-Vieira 2023, DMFR.
